title: Adaptive heartbeat thresholds for autoscaler stability and graceful failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We currently use fixed liveness/readiness probe thresholds and a simple health-signal->autoscaler mapping. During previous multi-region incidents, noisy probe failures and sudden traffic spikes caused autoscaler thrashing and unintended global failovers, which increased tail latency and led to SLO violations. Goal: Replace static probe thresholds with an adaptive heartbeat system that smooths signal inputs to the autoscaler, supports region-aware circuit breaking, and enables graceful load-shedding without violating per-route availability SLOs. Scope: health signal ingestion, adaptive threshold algorithm, probe multiplexing (reduce fan-out), autoscaler damping integration, region quorum checks for cross-region failover, and a staged rollout plan with canaries and synthetic spike testing.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive heartbeat algorithm reduces probe-driven autoscaler scale-in/scale-out events by >= 60% under synthetic noisy-probe scenarios
No increase in 99th percentile latency for hosted API routes beyond current SLO budget during canary (<= 5% regression threshold)
Region-level circuit breaker triggers and resolves according to configured SLO policies without causing global failover unless quorum is lost
Dashboard available showing raw probe rate, smoothed health score, autoscaler decisions, and load-shedding events
Runbook updated with new triage steps for adaptive-heartbeat related incidents
tasks: Design adaptive heartbeat algorithm and parameters (smoothing window, anomaly detector, per-tenant baseline)
Implement probe multiplexing layer to reduce fan-out to health-collector (server side agent + sidecar)
Integrate smoothed health score into autoscaler decision path with damping and hysteresis
Add region quorum logic and region-circuit-breaker service to the routing layer
Create synthetic fault-injection harness and benchmarking scripts
Build Grafana dashboards and SLO alert rules
Write runbook and rollout plan; coordinate with SRE and Product
decisions: Use EWMA smoothing + percentile baseline per route to compute adaptive threshold (decision reviewed 2026-03-11)
Probe multiplexing implemented in host agent rather than changing per-app probes to minimize app changes
Autoscaler damping: introduce a configurable scale cooldown derived from smoothed health rate instead of a fixed cooldown
Circuit breaker semantics: region enters 'degraded' when smoothed health < 0.7 for 3 consecutive evaluation windows; global failover requires >=2 region degraded (quorum)
Initial rollout will target non-critical models/low-traffic routes in eu-west-1 for canary
experiments: Synthetic noisy-probe test (2026-03-12): introduced random 5-20% probe failures for 30s across 100 instances. Result: baseline autoscaler triggered 18 scale events; adaptive-heartbeat prototype triggered 4 scale events and reduced control-plane ops by 78%

Traffic spike test (2026-03-13): simulated 3x QPS for 90s with cold KV caches. Result: with adaptive threshold and short-term cache-warm readiness gating, p95 latency rose by 9% but p99 stayed within SLO after tuning damping parameters
Multi-region failover simulation scheduled 2026-03-20 (planned) to validate quorum logic and controlled load-shedding
monitoring: Add metric: service.adaptive_heartbeat.smoothed_score (0-1) per route and region
Add metric: service.probe.raw_failure_rate per host and aggregated per route
Add metric: autoscaler.decision_count_by_cause (probe, cpu, rps, custom)
SLO dashboards: map smoothed_score trends to error budget burn and correlate with autoscaler actions
Alerting: create a P1 alert if smoothed_score < 0.5 for > 2 minutes in >=2 regions
